chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man with whom another man had pledged two slaves as collateral, and one of them perished. Would his right be in the other? He said: Yes. I said: Or a house, and it burned down—would his right be in the land? He said: Yes. I said: Or two animals, and one of them perished—would his right be in the other? He said: Yes. I said: Or goods that perished because of how long he left them, or food that spoiled, or a غلام whom smallpox struck and he became blind, or clothes that he left folded, not checking them and not unfolding them until they were ruined? He said: This is all one kind; his right remains upon him.

key_terms.التُّرْبَةِ: the land or ground remaining after the house burned
key_terms.جُدَرِيٌّ: smallpox, causing bodily harm in the example
key_terms.حَقُّهُ: his established legal right or claim
key_terms.دَارًا: a house used here as pledged property
key_terms.طَعَامًا: food that may spoil while held

ai.seo_question: If part of collateral is destroyed or spoiled, does the creditor's right still remain in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings of rahn, showing that when part of pledged property is lost, destroyed, or damaged, the creditor's right does not vanish. The ruling treats these cases as one category, affirming the continuing financial claim in relation to the remaining pledged value or liability.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4113 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who narrated from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, who narrated from Abu Abdillah (as):

I asked him about a man who took two slaves as collateral (rahn) from another man, and one of them perished. Does his right apply to the other slave?
Imam (as) said: "Yes."
I asked: What if it was a house that burned down? Does his right remain in the land?
Imam (as) said: "Yes."
I asked: What if it was two animals and one of them perished? Does his right apply to the other?
Imam (as) said: "Yes."
I asked: What if it was merchandise that was destroyed because it was left for a long time, or food that spoiled, or a servant who became blind due to smallpox, or clothes that were left folded without being aired out until they were ruined?
Imam (as) said: "All of this is the same case. His right remains applicable to the remaining property."
